primitives.name: Field Line Clustering
primitives.verbatim_quote: The presented method first detects reliable field lines from the camera image through clustering.
primitives.assumptions: Lines in image are segmented via spatial clustering of edge features; dominant lines are selected based on cumulative segment length.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure when lighting or occlusion obscures line segments, leading to incomplete or misclustered line sets.

layer2.mapping: Clustering kernel maps local line segments to global field structure via centroid-based grouping; supports downstream geometric correspondence.
layer2.telemetry: Number of detected clusters, average cluster size, and intra-cluster variance.

primitives.name: Directional Feature Matching
primitives.verbatim_quote: Constructing a novel directional feature of the intersection points of the lines in both the camera image and the model, the presented method then finds matching pairs of these points between the image and the model.
primitives.assumptions: Intersection points possess unique directional descriptors; matching is achieved via similarity in angular orientation and spatial proximity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure when directional features are ambiguous due to low contrast or overlapping lines.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic transformation between image and model intersection points preserves geometric relationships under affine projection.
layer2.telemetry: Matching pair count, angular deviation threshold, and descriptor similarity score.

primitives.name: Homography Estimation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Finally, Homography matrix estimations and validations are performed using the obtained matching pairs, which can reduce the required number of Homography matrix calculations.
primitives.assumptions: At least four non-collinear point pairs exist; estimation employs minimal set sampling for robustness.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure when insufficient or poorly distributed point pairs lead to ill-conditioned matrix inversion.

layer2.mapping: Kernel computes planar projective transformation matrix from matched point sets; validation ensures consistency across subsets.
layer2.telemetry: Condition number of homography matrix, reprojection error, and number of RANSAC iterations.

primitives.name: Extended Point Matching
primitives.verbatim_quote: Our presented method uses possible intersection points outside image for the point matching.
primitives.assumptions: Points beyond image boundary retain geometric relevance; their inclusion enhances estimation stability.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure when extrapolated points introduce systematic bias or noise in the matching process.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic extension of point domain from image to extended space allows full-field coverage in estimation.
layer2.telemetry: Percentage of external vs internal matches, mean distance from image border, and estimation error reduction.

The method begins with field line detection through clustering of line segments, identifying dominant vertical and horizontal lines. These lines define intersection points in both image and model spaces. A directional feature vector is constructed at each intersection point, capturing angular orientation and spatial context. Matching pairs are identified by minimizing angular and positional discrepancies. The homography matrix is then computed using these pairs, leveraging RANSAC to mitigate outliers. By incorporating points outside the image, the method increases robustness against projection errors. The key insight is that the geometric structure of the soccer field—its lines and intersections—is preserved under planar projection, enabling accurate registration. Failure modes include poor line detection due to illumination or occlusion, incorrect clustering leading to spurious lines, and mismatching due to ambiguous directional features. The method's strength lies in its modular design: clustering ensures reliable input, directional matching improves accuracy, and extended point usage stabilizes estimation.
